description: Cross-language conformance fixture catalog. NOTE: the $schema above is editor/IDE only — sce-build/src/conformance.rs hand-rolls runtime validation; the JSON schema is never consulted at codegen time. Each entry declares a fixture's structural metadata (kind, arg types, output shape) so sce-codegen can render per-language test harnesses from a single source. The oracle values — expected outputs — live in numerical_reference.json. Adding a new fixture requires (1) an SCXML file under tests/forge/resources/, (2) an entry here, and (3) an expected-value entry in numerical_reference.json. No language-specific test code should ever need to be hand-written.

kinds.interpolation: Pure lookup table with numeric interpolation. Struct::lookup(args) -> scalar. Reference section: pure_functions.
kinds.transform: Pure value transform. Free function(s) compute_*(args) -> scalar or multi-output. Reference section: pure_functions.
kinds.condition: Pure boolean predicate. Free function <name>(args) -> bool. Reference section: pure_functions.
kinds.filter: Stateful signal filter. Instance::update(input) -> output, one output per sequence step. Reference section: stateful_filters.
kinds.observer: Stateful event observer. Instance::update(input) -> event queue, zero-or-more events per step. Reference section: observers.
kinds.procedure: Pure procedure result. Language-specific binding returns ProcedureResult{completed, final_state}. Reference section: pure_functions.
kinds.lookup: Finite key→value mapping with on-miss=error policy. Free function lookup_<name>(key) -> Option<V>. Numeric output only — string outputs go through the existing enum-dispatch lookup path tested by forge_conformance goldens. Reference section: pure_functions.
kinds.validator: Stateful data validator. Instance::validate(args...) -> ValidationResult{valid, reason}. Internal sample memory (for rate-of-change checks) advances only on a successful validation, so oracle sequences exercise range / ROC / plausibility branches and the state-non-update rule. Reference section: validators.

canonical_types.description: Canonical arg/input/output types. Each per-language template maps these to its own type system (e.g. u16 -> uint16 in Go, UShort in Kotlin, std::uint16_t in C++).
